findings.finding: The example sets W={w} and V(p)=empty and immediately asserts non-reflexivity and vacuous Box p, but does not specify R. Both assertions require the empty relation on the one-world domain; a self-loop instead makes the relation reflexive and Box p false.
findings.controlling_evidence: On the sole world, the only possible accessibility edge is (w,w). With R empty, Box p is vacuously true and p false.
findings.required_translation_handling: State in adjacent Telugu prose that the accessibility relation has no pairs, with a visible source-correction note; keep the frozen English source.

findings.finding: The proposition requires Ruv and Rvu but does not rule out Ruu or Rvv, then concludes that the model is irreflexive. The listed cross-edges alone do not entail absence of self-loops.
findings.controlling_evidence: Taking R exactly {(u,v),(v,u)} and equal atomic valuations makes u and v modally indistinguishable by formula induction, yields all T instances at both worlds, and makes the relation irreflexive.
findings.required_translation_handling: Explicitly restrict the intended example to the two listed cross-edges, with an adjacent source-correction note; do not strengthen the general theorem beyond this example.
